page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-64 is a compute-oriented cloud instance driven by Google's Arm-based architecture. Powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz with one thread per core, the machine provides 128 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an 80 MB shared L3 cache, backed by hardware AES encryption acceleration. The instance does not feature attached local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring persistent network volumes for non-volatile storage.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier parallel execution and caching capabilities. The instance scored 26,801.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 116,240.18 in stress-ng multi-core testing, reaching top-decile ranks in Clang software compilation (85,520.0) and PassMark physics calculations (17,878.79). Memory subsystem performance is similarly robust, demonstrating 7,912.85 GB/sec in small-block cached read bandwidth and 190.24 GB/sec in uncached write throughput. Application-layer benchmarks reflect this throughput with 134.13 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 123.05 GB/sec in static web serving.

The 1:2 core-to-memory configuration delivers high compute density per dollar for CPU-bound pipelines, though workloads requiring heavy working memory footprints per thread will encounter capacity ceilings. The lack of onboard NVMe storage necessitates external storage considerations for IOPS-sensitive applications. Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-64 is well suited for parallel build systems, continuous integration pipelines, batch compute jobs, microservices hosting, and high-concurrency web serving infrastructure.

It pairs 128 GB of RAM with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, backed by 80 MB of L3 cache and hardware AES acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded processing, leading results in Clang compilation and PassMark physics, alongside over 134 million Redis SET operations per second and 123 GB/sec static web throughput. Memory bandwidth is pronounced, delivering 7,912 GB/sec in cached reads. Without bundled local storage or discrete GPUs, data persistence relies on network-attached storage. The hardware design yields high compute density and cost efficiency for CPU-intensive parallel jobs, software compilation, CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservices, and high-throughput web serving.
